name: The DAO
technique: Recursive call in splitDAO before balance update
rootCause: splitDAO() sent ETH to the caller before zeroing their balance. The attacker's fallback re-entered splitDAO recursively, draining 3.6M ETH into a child DAO. Ethereum hard-forked to return the funds, splitting off Ethereum Classic. It made checks-effects-interactions a standard rule.

descriptions.text: splitDAO() sent ETH to the caller before zeroing their balance. The attacker's fallback re-entered splitDAO recursively, draining 3.6M ETH into a child DAO. Ethereum hard-forked to return the funds, splitting off Ethereum Classic. It made checks-effects-interactions a standard rule.
The DAO smart contract running on the Ethereum suffered a reentrancy-attack-on-smart-contract.

On June 17, 2016, The DAO contract on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited via a reentrancy bug in its splitDAO function, allowing an attacker to recursively withdraw funds and drain approximately 3.6 million ETH (worth about $60 million at the time) into a child DAO. The community responded by executing a hard fork to recover most user funds, establishing critical lessons for smart contract security and governance. The splitDAO function transferred ether to the caller before zeroing their token balance, allowing a malicious contract to repeatedly re-enter the withdrawal process and extract funds multiple times.
